$comment: The wire-contract drift task U0.1 deliberately left behind, and the exact
set of test files it left failing. Read scripts/known-drift-gate.mjs for
how this file is used; read it before adding an entry.
Task U0.1 (2026-08-31, commit 6bf58f0) re-sourced wui/contract/ from
published Core v0.7.0 sessionwire/v1 -- 33 schemas, 33 fixtures -- and
removed Harness from the module graph. @looprig/client's TypeScript
schema mirror still describes the Harness-era wire contract, so it
disagrees with the newly mirrored Core contract. The Wave 2 checkpoint
permits that drift; reconciling it is Wave 4C protocol work and is blocked
on Factory contract fixtures that do not exist yet.
This is an allowance for a KNOWN, DATED, BOUNDED failure, not a way to stop
running the suite. It records four things, and the gate asserts all four:
suiteFiles -- every test file the suite is expected to RUN, mapped to the
number of tests it is expected to COLLECT. The gate fails if the set vitest
reports differs in either direction, and if any file's count differs.
Both halves were added because the thing above them was PRINTED and not
asserted: the first gate printed "26 of 36 test files pass" and asserted
nothing about the 36, so a file renamed out of vitest's include glob
stopped guarding at exit 0; pinning the names left the same hole one level
in, so deleting one passing `it` from test/blocks.test.ts (24 -> 23) also
exited 0. A collected count is a property of the source, not of a server or
a timeout, so this applies to the three HTTP files too -- verified
identical for all 36 files across independent full runs.
fileGranular -- the ONLY files exempt from per-test gating. This is the
pinned partition, checked in both directions, because a shape check that
merely demanded one of two fields was satisfied by a free-text string:
replacing test/contract.test.ts's 58-name set with granularityReason
"flaky" exited 0 and left that file's 62 tests ungated for the rest of the
allowance. Moving a file here is a deliberate edit to this list, not the
deletion of a field.
files[*].failingTests -- for the seven drifted files that are fast and
deterministic, the exact set of failing test names. A NEW failure inside a
drifted file is a name not on the list and fails the gate.
files[*].granularityReason -- for the three files in fileGranular, why.
Each says so for itself rather than sharing one blanket justification,
because the earlier blanket version was true of these three and was applied
to all ten.
The gate fails if a file listed in files stops failing, so retiring an entry
is a deliberate edit in the same commit that fixes the drift.

2026-09-25 (wui v0.4.0): core v0.12.0 adds eight principal/metadata schema-and-fixture pairs; their Harness-era allSchemas mirrors fail like the older Core schemas, while factorySchemas is their real command-plane mirror.
STATED COST, and it is now the only one: inside the three fileGranular HTTP
files a new failure is not distinguished from the drift. Which files run, how
many tests each contains, and which tests fail in the other seven are all
asserted.
